description: Democratization, state-building and economic reform; creation of new institutions; impacts of Soviet rule.

title: Politics in Israel
description: Introduction to the domestic politics of Israel in comparative perspective, including issues of internal cultural diversity, religion and politics, fragmentation of the political party system, and coalition governance.

title: Contemp African Politics
description: African politics since the end of the Cold War. Topics include: Strategic Security Approach, Democratization, Human Rights, HIV/AIDS, African Peacekeeping, Terrorism, Religious and Ethnic Conflict, Debt and Stalled Development.

title: Development in Africa
description: Political and economic development within Sub-Saharan Africa. States and institutions, democracy, party systems, military coups/rule, bureaucracy/corruption, race/ethnicity, national/regional integrations, trade unions, economic development strategies, class formation, and women's roles and ideology.

title: West European Politics
description: The evolution, politics, and contemporary problems of selected political systems of Western Europe.

title: British Politics
description: The evolution, politics, and contemporary problems of Britain's political system.

title: French Politics
description: The evolution, politics and contemporary problems of France's political system.

title: German Politics
description: Evolution, politics and contemporary problems of Germany's political system.

title: East Asia: China
description: Evolution of political institutions and political culture in China with emphasis on the post-1949 period. Primary attention to nationalism, modernization and political efficacy.

title: Japanese Politics
description: Japanese politics, with an emphasis on the postwar period. Particular emphasis on political parties, elections, political economy, and social problems.

title: Southeast Asian Politics
description: Evolution of political institutions and economy of selected nations in Southeast Asia. Emphasis on imperialist legacy, nation building in multi-ethnic communities, and contrasts in economic performance.

title: Judicial Politics
description: Politics of judicial policy making , issues surrounding constitutional interpretation and decision making, prerequisite for courses on the politics of constitutional law.

title: Constitutional Politics
description: The constitutional politics surrounding such issues as the right to free expression, associational rights, the right to free exercise of religious beliefs and the right to privacy.

title: Politics of Equality
description: Constitutional politics of equality in the American political system; issues surrounding constitutional doctrine and judicial policymaking; special attention on racial and sexual equality.

title: Const & Justice Sys
description: Constitutional politics of the American criminal justice system. Issues surrounding constitutional doctrine and judicial policymaking on issues such as search and seizure. Arrest, trial, incarceration and other issues of due process.

title: Legal Philosophy
description: Analysis of the nature and functions of law; law as an instrument of social control and the relationship between law and morality.

title: Jud Proc & Behav
description: Analysis of the behavior of judges and courts in the political process. Techniques of judicial decision making. Relationships among courts and other decision-making bodies.

title: Voting Rights
description: Examination of recent issues, political battles, policy, and legal decisions on voting rights in the United States.

title: Amer Pol Parties
description: Analysis of the structured operations of the party system in the United States; party functions and organizations, nomination processes, campaigns and elections, party trends and reforms.

title: Rules of Electoral Game
description: Not available.

title: Elec & Voting Behavior
description: Analysis of American elections and partisan behavior; political socialization, political participation, partisanship and individual and group determinants of voting.

title: Group Politics
description: Groups, institutions and individuals, especially in American politics. Historical and analytical treatment of group theories as applied to interest groups (especially labor, business, agriculture, science, military); to racial, ethnic and sectional groups; to parties, public and legislative groups, bureaucracies.

title: Public Opinion
description: Nature of public opinion in America as it is supposed to be and as it is. Distribution of opinions among different publics and the significance of that distribution for system stability and institutions. Opinion polling and its problems.

title: Mass Media & Politics
description: Organization of and decision making within the media; media audiences and the effect of the media on attitudes and behavior; the relationship of the government to the media (censorship, secrecy, freedom of the press, government regulation);the media in election campaigns.

title: Mass Media & Politics
description: Organization of and decision making within the media; media audiences and the effect of the media on attitudes and behavior; the relationship of the government to the media (censorship, secrecy, freedom of the press, government regulation);the media in election campaigns

title: Women In Politics
description: The role of women in American politics. Historical experiences; contemporary organizations and strategies; areas of legislative concern; the impact of differences in social class, race, and ethnicity upon the involvement of women in politics.

title: Intersectional Politics
description: Examination of political attitudes and behaviors of groups at the intersection of multiple marginalized identities.

title: Latino Politics
description: Political aspects of Chicano life in America; examines the Chicano's political role as it has been historically defined by different groups in society and the Chicano's responses to his/her political environment.

title: Immigration Politics US
description: Examination of contemporary issues, political rhetoric and election outcomes, policy choices and legal decisions on immigration politics in the United States.

title: Political Psychology
description: Overview to the growing literature on political psychology. Introduction to how psychological concepts (personality, attitudes, stereotypes, heuristics, affect, identity, group dynamics) help us understand how citizens think about politics.

title: Politics Of Energy
description: Nature and performance of political processes for making energy choices at the international, national and state levels. Interaction of energy policy with other political goals and the ability of governmental institutions to overcome constraints on policy innovation.

title: Amer Political Developmt
description: Systematic analysis of contemporary issues in American political development: historical determinants of political change; the timing and character of institutional development; conditions for successful political action. Democratization, cultural change, party formation, state-building, constitutionalism, race relations.

title: Political Economy
description: Political basis of economic policy (taxation, spending and regulation); impact of prices, employment and growth on political demands; elite responses to economic conditions; policy alternatives and the public interest.

title: Science, Technology
description: Analysis of policymaking for science and the use of scientific expertise for making decisions about technology. Topics include funding of basic research, relationship of science to technological development, science and military policy, technological risks, technology assessment and scientists and politics.

title: Racial Politics
description: Race, racial attitudes and racial policies in the United States with a specific emphasis on African Americans.

title: Spec Stdy Comp Pol
description: Intensive examination of one or more special problems appropriate to comparative politics. Coverage is given to formal and informal political institutions, economically developing and developed countries, and non-democratic, democratic, and democratizing countries.

title: Bureaucracy/Mod Soc
description: Role of bureaucracy in a complex society,with emphasis upon changing relationships between government and the economy; consequences of rapid technological and social change for bureaucratic structures and processes; the problems of reconciling expertise and democracy and increasing the responsiveness of public bureaucracy.
prerequisite: Consent of Instructor. POL 001 or POL 002 recommended.

title: Administrative Behavior
description: The implications for American public administration of evolving concepts about behavior in organizations.

title: Administrative Theory
description: Historical and critical analysis of the principal theories of organization and management of public agencies in light of such concepts as decision making, bureaucracy, authority and power, communication and control; examination of role of government bureaucracies in the total society.

title: Intl Relations
description: Analysis and evaluation of substantive issues in contemporary international relations. Readings drawn from current academic and non-academic periodicals.

title: Internship Pub Aff
description: Supervised internship and study in political, governmental, or related organizations.
prerequisite: Consent of Instructor. Highest priority assigned to students with Political Science Public Service major; upper division standing required.

title: Internship Pub Aff
description: Supervised internship and study in political, governmental, or related organizations.
prerequisite: POL 192A; Consent of Instructor. Highest priority assigned to students with Political Science-Public Service major; upper division standing.

title: Res In Practical Pol
description: Supervised preparation of an extensive paper relating internship experience to concepts, literature, and theory of political science.
prerequisite: POL 192A; POL 192B; open only to Political Science-Public Service majors, for whom it is required.

title: Washington Ctr Research
description: Core academic component of Washington Program. Topics coordinated with internships. Research draws on resources uniquely available in Washington, DC. Supervised preparation of extensive paper.

title: Special Stdy Honors
description: Directed reading, research and writing culminating in preparation of a senior honors thesis under the direction of faculty advisor.
prerequisite: Major in Politcal Science with upper division standing and a GPA of 3.500 in the major.

title: Special Stdy Honors
description: Directed reading, research and writing culminating in preparation of a senior honors thesis under the direction of faculty advisor.
prerequisite: Major in Political Science with upper division standing and a GPA of 3.500 in the major.

title: Spec Study Am Pol
description: Intensive examination of one or more special problems appropriate to American politics.
prerequisite: Consent of Instructor. Upper division standing.

title: Amer Politics Seminar
description: Intensive reading, discussion, research, writing in American politics. Topics may include Congress, the Presidency, the Supreme Court, federalism, voting behavior, interest groups, ethnic groups or other topics with a more specialized content than normal course offerings.
prerequisite: Upper division Political Science majors or consent of instructor.

title: Comparative Pol Seminar
description: Intensive reading, discussion, research, writing in comparative politics. Topics may include one country or geographical area, political institutions or behavior across countries, political development, or other topics that are more specialized than normal course offerings.
prerequisite: Upper division Political Science majors or consent of instructor.

title: Internat'l Relations Sem
description: Intensive reading, discussion, research, writing in international relations including study of international political institutions (UN, EU, or NATO) or interstate relations (war, trade, immigration) and other topics with more specialized content than normal course offerings.
prerequisite: Upper division Political Science majors or consent of instructor.

title: Political Theory Seminar
description: Intensive reading, discussion, research, writing in political theory. Topics may include study of a single political thinker, a group of related thinkers, development of political concepts, or other topics with more specialized content than normal course offerings.
prerequisite: Upper division Political Science majors or consent of instructor.

title: Research Methods Seminar
description: Intensive reading, discussion, research, and writing in selected topics in Research Methods such as research design, statistics, game theory, etc.
prerequisite: Upper division Political Science majors or consent of instructor.

title: Tutoring in Pol Sci
description: Tutor responsibilities such as attending class, offering a guest lecture on a select topic, assisting in group discussions, hosting consultation or review sessions, or assisting instructor with assignments (though not grading).

title: Fruit Production
description: Field trip seventh Saturday of quarter (1/2 day). Biological and environmental principles of tree-crop agriculture emphasizing California production. Topics include temperate and subtropical species, biotechnology and genetic improvement, environmental physiology, plant and crop growth, pest and disease control, consumer issues.

title: Tropical Ecology
description: Course in Panama. Sustainable agricultural systems to protect tropical rainforest ecosystems, sustainable agriculture in the Panama Canal watershed, language and culture of Panama and the U.S.A.

title: Elementary Portuguese
description: Introduction to Portuguese grammar and development of all language skills in a cultural context with special emphasis on communication.

title: Elementary Portuguese
description: Continuation of course 001 in the areas of grammar and development of all basic language skills in cultural context with special emphasis on communication.

title: Elementary Portuguese
description: Continuation of course 002 in the areas of grammar and development of all basic language skills in cultural context with special emphasis on communication.

title: Elem Port Conversation
description: Designed to develop oral communication skills. Emphasis on increasing vocabulary, improving listening comprehension, pronunciation, accuracy and grammar control. Practice of everyday situations.

title: Intermediate Portuguese
description: Review and develop the grammar, vocabulary, and composition acquired in first year Portuguese through exercises and reading of modern texts.

title: Intermediate Portuguese
description: Continuation of course 21. Focus on more difficult grammar concepts and further composition practice. Development of all language skills through exercises and reading of modern texts.

title: Portuguese Composition I
description: Development of writing skills by way of reading, discussion, and analysis of authentic materials, literary texts, and videos. Selective review of grammar. Class activities include composition, journals, letters, individual and group projects.

title: LusoBrazilian Lit & Crit
description: Principles of literary criticism applied to the study of fiction, poetry, and essays of major literary writers of the Luso-Brazilian world.
prerequisite: POR 022 or POR 023; or Consent of Instructor.

title: Topics in Luso-Brazilian
description: Special topics in the study of Luso-Brazilian literature and culture.

title: Luso-Braz Lit & Culture
description: Colonial Brazilian literature survey. Readings include 16th-18th centuries manuscripts and books of cultural importance in a society dominated by censorship and with no printing presses. Study of the role literary Academies played in the so called "culture of manuscripts."

title: Intro to Braz Literature
description: Narrative and poetic texts of the 19th and 20th centuries in Brazil. In-depth and comparative study of Romantic and (Neo)Naturalist movements as a forum for discussion about literary tradition and modernity in Latin America.

title: 20thC Mstrs in Braz Lit
description: Overview of modern Brazilian literature from early 20th C to the poetry by Jo?????o Cabral de Melo Neto and the Concretists (1960s), including European avant-garde movements and literary and cultural manifestos leading to a revolutionary body of literature.

title: Directed Gp Study
description: Directed group study.
prerequisite: Consent of instructor and Department Chairperson.

title: Spec Stud for Adv Under
description: Independent study with professor for advanced undergraduate students, or honor thesis students.

title: General Psychology
description: Introduction emphasizing empirical approaches. Focus on perception, cognition, personality and social psychology, and biological aspects of behavior.

title: General Psychology
description: Introduction to empirical approaches. Focus on perception, cognition, personality and social psychology, and biological aspects of behavior.

title: General Psychology
description: Introduction to empirical approaches. Focus on perception, cognition, personality and social psychology, and biological aspects of behavior.

title: Data Visualization
description: Introduction to quantitative data across the social sciences (Communications, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, and other disciplines). Transforming data, describing data, producing graphs, visual reasoning, and interpretations.

title: Research Meth in Psych
description: Introduction to experimental design, interviews, questionnaires, field and observational methods, reliability, and statistical inference.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); PSC 012Y, STA 013 or STA 013Y or STA 013V or STA 100 strongly recommended.

title: Research Meth in Psych
description: Introduction to experimental design, interviews, questionnaires, field and observational methods, reliability, and statistical inference.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); PSC 012Y or STA 013 or STA 013Y or STA 013V or STA 100 strongly recommended.

title: Relationship Science
description: Evolutionary perspectives on attraction and close relationships. Integrating social psychological and evolutionary theories with empirical evidence pertaining to human mating.
prerequisite: PSC 001 or PSC 001Y; or introductory social science course or introductory life science course.

title: Stat Analys Psych Data
description: Design and statistical analysis of psychological investigations and the interpretation of quantitative data in psychology.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V)

title: Stat Analys Psych Data
description: Probability theory, sampling distributions, hypothesis testing, statistical inference, one-way and two-way analysis of variance, nonparametric statistics, with applications in psychology.

title: Applied Psychrometrics
description: Examination of the basic principles and applications of classical and modern test theory. Topics include test construction, reliability theory, validity theory, factor analysis and latent trait theory.
prerequisite: (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); PSC 103A; (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y); Upper division standing in Psychology.

title: Network Analysis in PSC
description: Fundamental principles of Graph Theory and applications of Network Analysis to psychological data. Community detection, network control, and modeling of cascading failures.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 103A)

title: Quest & Survey Methods
description: Introduction to survey and questionnaire research methods with emphasis on how to ask questions. Social and psychological factors that influence survey response. Practical aspects of fielding survey and questionnaire research.
prerequisite: PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y; and Consent of Instructor. PSC 041 or an equivalent course on social or behavioral research methods or consent of instructor.

title: Psych of Soc Devel
description: Theory and research on social development from childhood to adulthood. Topics include the development of personality, achievement motivation, self-understanding, sex-role identity, and antisocial behavior, with an emphasis on the interface between biological and social factors. Only 2 units of credit allowed to students who have completed Human Development 102.

title: Agent-Based Modeling
description: Introduction to agent-based computer simulation and analysis with emphasis on learning how to model animals, including humans, to achieve insight into social and group behavior.

title: Language & Cognition
description: Introduction to the cognitive processes involved in language comprehension and production. Topics include the biological foundations of language, speech perception, word recognition, syntax, reading ability, and pragmatics.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 100 or PSC 100Y or PSC 135); or Consent of Instructor.

title: Neuroeconomics&Decisions
description: Theory and research on memory development with focus on infancy and childhood.
prerequisite: (PSC 100 or PSC 100Y or PSC 135 or ARE 100A or ECN 100A or ECN 100AV or NPB 162 or NPB 163); (STA 013 or STA 013V or STA 013Y or STA 100 or PSC 103A); or Consent of Instructor.

title: Psych of Music
description: Introduction to the mental and neural representations of musical structures and processes involved in perceiving, remembering, and performing music. Music and emotion.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 100 or PSC 100Y or PSC 135 or MUS 006C); or Consent of Instructor.

title: Advanced Cog Neuro
description: Advanced integrative survey of cognitive neuroscience, including perception, attention, memory, and navigation. Emphasis on reviewing literature in psychology, neuroscience, and statistics; understanding methods in cognition; and presentation skills.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); PSC 135; or Consent of Instructor.

title: Cognitive Development
description: Theories, methods, evidence, and debates in the field of cognitive development, such as nature/nurture, constraints on learning, and the role of plasticity. Topics include attention, memory, concepts about the physical and social world, and language.
prerequisite: PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV

title: Social & Personal Devel
description: Social and personality development of children, infancy through adolescence. Topics include the development of personality, achievement motivation, self-understanding, sex-role identity, and antisocial behavior. Emphasis on the interface between biological and social factors.
prerequisite: PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or HDE 100A or HDE 100AV or HDE 100B or HDE 100BV

title: Environ Awarness
description: Interactions of people with built environments. Research methods for evaluating designed environments and reviews of current research in environmental psychology.

title: Developmental Cog Neuro
description: Behavior of the individual in the group. Examination of basic psychological processes in social situations, surveying various problems of social interaction: group tensions, norm-development, attitudes, values, public opinion, status.
prerequisite: PSC 135 or ((PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V or HDE 100A or HDE 100B); (PSC 101 or PSC 121 or NPB 161 or HDE 163)); PSC 141 recommended.

title: Development of Memory
description: Theory and research on memory development with focus on infancy and childhood.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 140 or PSC 140V or PSC 140Y or PSC 141 or PSC 142 or PSC 100 or PSC 130)

title: Personality Theory
description: The theories of Freud, Erikson, and other major twentieth-century approaches to personality.

title: Relationship Science
description: Advanced integrative survey of biological principles of behavioral organization, emphasizing historical roots, current research directions, conceptual issues and controversies. Laboratory exercises on the description and analysis of the behavior of captive and free-living animals (Same course as Neurobiology, Physiology, and Behavior 150.)
prerequisite: PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y; PSC 041 recommended.

title: Relationship Science
description: Evolutionary perspectives on attraction and close relationships. Integrating social psychological and evolutionary theories with empirical evidence pertaining to human mating.
prerequisite: PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y; PSC 041 recommended.

title: Social Psychology
description: Behavior of the individual in the group. Examination of basic psychological processes in social situations, surveying various problems of social interaction: group tensions, norm-development, attitudes, values, public opinion, status.
prerequisite: PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y, PSC 041 recommended

title: Social Psychology
description: Behavior of the individual in the group. Examination of basic psychological processes in social situations, surveying various problems of social interaction: group tensions, norm-development, attitudes, values, public opinion, status.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V) and PSC 041 recommended.

title: Cultural Appropriation
description: Interactions of people and the environments they construct. Research methods for evaluating designed environments and reviews of current research in environmental psychology.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V)

title: Psych of Diversity Aging
description: Survey of interrelationships among psychological processes, interpersonal dynamics, and organizational forms. Topics include motivation, communication, decision making, leadership, personnel selection and training, stress and conflict, career development, organizational development, and organization-community relations.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001Y or PSC 001V); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); (PSC 140 or PSC 140Y or PSC 140V); or Consent of Instructor.

title: Ster, Prej, & Stigma
description: Social psychological underpinnings of stereotyping, prejudice, and stigma from sociocultural, motivational, and cognitive perspectives. Topics include: origins, maintenance, change, effects on person perception and memory, and the automaticity/controllability of stereotyping and prejudice.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V)

title: Prej Sexual Orientation
description: Current scientific knowledge about sexual orientation and prejudice based on sexual orientation. Emphasis is placed on learning the skills necessary for a critical understanding of science and public policy issues relevant to sexuality.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V)

title: Personality Psychology
description: The theories of Freud, Erikson, and other major twentieth-century contemporary approaches to personality.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V)

title: Personality Theory
description: The theories of Freud, Erikson, and other major twentieth-century contemporary approaches to personality.

title: Mental Health & Illness
description: Descriptive and functional account of behavioral disorders, with primary consideration given to neurotic and psychotic behavior.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V)

title: MultiCultural Psychology
description: Effects of culture and ethnicity on psychological processes, such as social cognition, emotion, motivation, personality, self-concept, and interpersonal behavior (i.e., how culture makes who you are). Individuals' construction of multicultural identity and experiences.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V)

title: Psychology of Religion
description: Major theories, issues, data, and research methodologies of the psychology of religion. Religious experience and expression; religious development in childhood, adolescence, and adulthood; conversion; religious influences on physical and mental health; cross-cultural perspectives.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V)

title: Genius & Creativity
description: Phenomenon of genius is examined from a diversity of theoretical, methodological, and disciplinary perspectives, with an emphasis on outstanding creativity and leadership in art, music, literature, philosophy, science, war, and politics.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); or equivalents, or consent of instructor.

title: Psychobiography
description: Case-history research as a non-quantitative approach to studying personality. Psychological interpretation of life histories of outstanding individuals in the arts, politics, science and other areas.

title: History of Psychology
description: Development of psychological thought and research in context of history of philosophy and science.
prerequisite: (PSC 001 or PSC 001V or PSC 001Y); (PSC 041 or PSC 041V); Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

title: Special Study for Honors
description: Directed research. Supervised reading, research and writing leading to submission of a Senior Honors thesis under the direction of faculty sponsor.
prerequisite: Consent of Instructor. senior standing in Psychology and qualifications for admission into college honors program; at least one course from PSC 180A, PSC 180B, PSC 180C or PSC 199 strongly recommended.

title: Elementary Punjabi
description: Introduction to listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in Punjabi and to Punjabi culture.

title: Elementary Punjabi
description: Introduction to listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in Punjabi and to Punjabi culture.

title: Elementary Punjabi
description: Continuation of PUN 001. Introduction to listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in Punjabi and to Punjabi culture.
prerequisite: PUN 001 or PUN 001V; or Consent of Instructor.

title: Elementary Punjabi
description: Continuation of PUN 001V. Introduction to listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in Punjabi and to Punjabi culture.
prerequisite: PUN 001 or PUN 001V; or Consent of Instructor.

title: Elementary Punjabi
description: Continuation of PUN 002. Introduction to listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in Punjabi and to Punjabi culture.
prerequisite: PUN 002 or PUN 002V; or Consent of Instructor.

title: Elementary Punjabi
description: Continuation of PUN 002V. Introduction to listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in Punjabi and to Punjabi culture.
prerequisite: PUN 002 or PUN 002V; or Consent of Instructor.

title: Intermediate Punjabi
description: Integrated listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in formal and informal contexts in Intermediate Punjabi. Continuation of fluency acquisition through grammar, vocabulary, and meaningful verbal and written expressions in Punjabi. Short readings and essays in Punjabi literature and culture.
prerequisite: PUN 003 or PUN 003V; or Consent of Instructor.

title: Intermediate Punjabi
description: Integrated listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in formal and informal contexts in Intermediate Punjabi. Continuation of fluency acquisition in grammar, vocabulary, and meaningful verbal and written expression in Punjabi. Short final essay about topics in Punjabi literature and culture.

title: Intermediate Punjabi
description: Integrated listening, speaking, reading, and writing skills in formal and informal contexts in Intermediate Punjabi. Greater comprehension and production of meaningful verbal and written expression in Punjabi. Final research project related to topics in Punjabi literature and culture.

title: Survey of Religion
description: Basic concepts introduced through readings of the primary religious literature. Discussion of central ideas (creation, history, law, prophecy, suffering, mysticism, asceticism, karma, reincarnation, moksha, etc.); readings from the Bible, Bhagavad Gita, the Koran, selections from Plato and early Buddhist writings.

title: Pilgrimage
description: Introduction to comparative religion, focusing on a particular theme in a number of religious traditions: (A) Pilgrimage.

title: Death & Afterlife
description: Introduction to the methods used in comparative religion, focusing on a particular theme in a number of religious traditions: (B) Death and After-life.

title: Sacrifice
description: Introduction to the methods used in comparative religion, focusing on a particular theme in a number of religious traditions: (C) Sacrifice.

title: Conversion
description: Introduction to the methods used in comparative religion, focusing on a particular theme in several religious traditions: (D) Conversion.

title: Fundamentalism
description: Introduction to comparative religion, focusing on a particular theme in a number of religious traditions: (E) Fundamentalism.

title: Religion Today
description: Introduction to the methods used in comparative religion, focusing on a particular theme in a number of religious traditions: (F) Contemporary Religion.

title: Myth Ritual Symbol
description: Myths, rituals and religious symbols found in a variety of religious traditions including examples from ancient and contemporary religious life. Variety of religious phenomena; validity of different approaches to the study of religion.

title: Sex, Marriage, Divorce
description: Methods used in the study of religion, focusing on a particular theme in a number of religious traditions.

title: Music, Voice, Word
description: Exploration of relation between religion and musical traditions in various cultures. Investigation of ways music, vocal performance and sound production reflect and shape modern religious sensibilities. Special attention to gender, ethnicity, race, class, nationalism, secularism and mass media.

title: Myth Ritual Symbol
description: Not available.

title: Exprntl Dmnsn:Pilgrimage
description: Introduction to the methods used in comparative religion, focusing on a particular theme in a number of religious traditions:(A)The Experiential Dimension:Pilgrimage;(B)The Mythic Dimension:Death and the After-life;(C)The Ritual Dimension:Sacrifice. May be repeated for credit in a different subject area.

title: Myth Dmnsn:Dth Aftr Life
description: Introduction to the methods used in comparative religion, focusing on a particular theme in a number of religious traditions:(A)The Experiential Dimension:Pilgrimage;(B)The Mythic Dimension:Death and the After-life;(C)The Ritual Dimension:Sacrifice. May be repeated for credit in a different subject area.

title: Ritual Dmnsn:Sacrifice
description: Introduction to the methods used in comparative religion, focusing on a particular theme in a number of religious traditions:(A)The Experiential Dimension:Pilgrimage;(B)The Mythic Dimension:Death and the After-life;(C)The Ritual Dimension:Sacrifice. May be repeated for credit in a different subject area.

title: Fundamentalism
description: Introduction to the global and comparative study of fundamentalism. Historical origins, basic texts, cultural context of fundamentalist strains of Christianity, Islam, Judaism, Hinduism. Emphasis on fundamentalism and science, terrorism, politics and gender.

title: Comp Religion
description: Comparative Religion based on rotating topics such as Dreams and Revelations, Evil, Prophecy, Salvation, and Crime and Punishment.

title: Intro Health Humanities
description: Humanities in the health sciences focusing on illness, the practice of medicine, and the role of culture in biomedical research.

title: Health & Religion
description: Ethical dilemmas in healthcare and religion. End of life, illness, responsibility for the common good, humanity??????s relationship to the natural world, growing up, birth, pregnancy, conception.

title: Ethics Issues
description: This course presents challenging, contemporary ethical issues from a multi-cultural perspective. Rotating topics will include Ethical Eating, Capital Punishment, Euthanasia, Poverty, and Animal Rights.

title: Ethical Issues
description: Discussion of the readings assigned for course 10 and completion of a major research paper.
prerequisite: RST 010 { can be concurrent }; RST 010 required concurrently; GE topical breadth and diversity credit only with concurrent enrollment in RST 010.

title: Ethical Eating
description: Introduction to the complex and varied ethical, religious, and cultural meanings that food has had across the centuries and globe.

title: Jews,Christians&Muslims
description: History of religion in the ancient Near East and Mediterranean, from the Persian period through the rise of Islam. Emphasis on historical and social contexts of the formation of new traditions, in particular Judaism, Christianity, and Islam.

title: Reading/Fighting War
description: Introduction to both classic religious texts about war and a set of actual scenarios drawn from the experience and training of soldiers in recent military conflicts.

title: The Bible
description: Selected texts from the Hebrew Scriptures (GenesisII Chronicles) and review of modern scholarship on the texts from a variety of perspectives (historical, literary, sociological, psychological). Course work is based on an English translation and no knowledge of Hebrew is required.

title: Intro To Judaism
description: Introduction to the study of religion using examples from the rituals, art and holy texts of Judaism. No prior knowledge of either Judaism or the study of religion is necessary.

title: South Asian Religions
description: Introduction to South Asian religions, including Hinduism, Buddhism, Islam, Jainism and Sikhism. Traces historical developments from Vedic texts and their ascetic reformulation by sages such as Yajnavalkya, Siddhartha Gautama, and Mahavira into our global present.

title: Intro to Jainism
description: Introduction to topics central to Jain tradition through critical, historical and ethical perspectives.

title: History of Yoga
description: History of yoga from antiquity to its most recent formulation in American popular and consumer culture.

title: Magic and Demons
description: Exploration of magic, demons, and other powers in South Asian religions from the ancient to the modern periods.

title: Introduction to Buddhism
description: Buddhism in its pan-Asian manifestations, from its beginning in India to its development in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia, Central Asia, China and Japan; teachings and practices, socio-political and cultural impact.

title: New Testament
description: New Testament literature from critical, historical, and theological perspectives.

title: Religion & Sci Fiction
description: Representations of actual and fictional religious movements in science fiction and fantasy writing and film. Examination of: the characteristics of religion and religiosity in fictional religious movements; the relationship between religion, science, and technology in modern speculative fiction.

title: Christianity
description: Major concepts and practices in the Christian tradition. Survey of the history of Christianity and Christian expansion from antiquity to modern times.

title: Intro to Islam
description: Introduction to topics central to the Islamic tradition. Muhammad, the Qur'an, Islamic law, theology, philosophy, cosmology, worship, and mysticism. Race and gender in Islam, Islamic revival, and varying experiences of Islam in different historical and cultural settings.

title: American Islam
description: Development of Islam in the United States of America. How Muslims have been integral to the making of the Americas and American identities for over four centuries. Musical and dance traditions, clothing and the ethics of material display, storytelling and poetry, and participation in struggles for civil and human rights.

title: The Qur'an
description: The Qur'an, its history, its various functions in the lives of Muslims, and its different interpretations. Quranic themes such as God and humankind, nature and revelation, eschatology and Satan. Islam and other religions; women, gender, and sexuality.

title: Bhagavad Gita
description: The Bhagavad Gita, its history and reception, and its significance in the lives of Hindus. Themes explored include Hindu theories of god, self, war, peace, duty, and action.

title: Modern Hinduism
description: Historical survey of modern Hinduism from the early-19th century to the present. Topics include Rammohun Roy, Sir William Jones, and Mahatma Gandhi, nationalism, post-colonialism and diasporic religion.

title: Hinduism
description: Hindu tradition from ancient to modern times. Multiplicity of religious forms within Hinduism with mention of Jainism, Buddhism, and Sikhism and their relation to the mainstream of Hindu religion.

title: Hindu Mythology
description: Survey of the major narrative traditions within Hinduism, including epic literature and local stories in oral, textual, visual and performative forms.

title: Religion & Language
description: Provides students with a basic toolkit for studying religious discourse in a variety of traditions. Concentrates on the sacred and profane, the wondrous and ordinary, the mystical and reasonable.

title: Plant Magic
description: Medicinal use of plants and fungi in religious worship. Co-evolution of herbs and humans. How sensory, intellectual, and experimental engagement with plants and fungi helps scholars and activists confront violence, colonialism, racial capitalism and modernity.

title: Religion, Gender, Sex
description: Constructions of gender and sexuality within one or more religious traditions, pre-modern and modern. Emphasis on the interaction between religious, medical, and ethical definitions of the human body and sexual behavior.

title: Religion American Pol
description: Introduction to the interdisciplinary study of the origins, evolution, denial and protection of Human Rights.

title: Issues & Methods
description: Principal issues and methods of Religious Studies and associated fields.

title: Christian Origins
description: Development of Christianity from the end of the first century through the major controversies of the fifth century. Emphasis on the relationship between the new religious movement and the Roman Empire, and issues of early Christian identity and diversity.

title: Med & Byzan Christianity
description: Christianity in Europe and the Near East from the year 600 to 1450. Focus on the development of Catholic and Orthodox traditions in ritual, art, and thought, with attention to interactions between regional groups, and Christian interaction with Islam.

title: Christianity 1450-1700
description: History of Reformation conflicts over the authority of scripture, the nature of man and the universe, and the basis of morality with the goal of understanding how these conflicts laid the foundation for the modern world.

title: Christianity & Modernity
description: Reaction of Christian critics and apologists to the profound cultural and scientific transformations resulting from the Scientific Revolution, the Enlightenment, and the advent of the modern critical study of religion.

title: Contemp Christianity
description: Christianity in the 20th and 21st centuries. Relationship of Christianity to globalization, industrialization, mass media, and the contemporary secular state. Focus on Christianity in developing nations and on the relationship of established Christian institutions to new Christian movements.

title: Meaning & Identity
description: Study of religious lives, the quest for meaning and for personal identity; how religions frame the problems of life; how cultural and personal crises affect youthful identity; the nature and structure of dreams, myths, and ideals.

title: Mysticism
description: Historical and descriptive analysis of selected key figures in mystical traditions and readings of representative mystical texts. Analytic term paper.
prerequisite: One lower division Religious Studies course.

title: Religion Magic & Science
description: Religion, magic, and science from the middle ages to the present. Contrast between modern scientific methodology and religious and magical thinking.

title: Biblical Texts
description: Study of a book from the Prophets or writings from critical, historical, and religious perspectives.

title: Sex & Gender in Bible
description: Gender and sexuality in the Bible and its interpretation in Judaism and Christianity. Femininity and masculinity; gender roles; homosexuality; sexual violence. Historical origins in the ancient world; influence on contemporary views.

title: Dead Sea Scrolls
description: Survey of the Dead Sea Scrolls, apocryphal and pseudepigraphical writings of Judaism and Christianity and their historical, social, and religious importance.

title: Rabbinics
description: Survey of the classical rabbinic Jewish texts such as the Talmud and of the social and historical contexts of their production in Palestine and Babylonia.

title: Topics Rel Studies
description: Thematic study of a phenomenon in more than one religious tradition or of the relationship between religion and another cultural phenomenon. Topics may include archeology and the Bible, women and religion, religion and violence.
prerequisite: RST 001 or RST 002 or RST 003A or RST 003B or RST 003C; or Consent of Instructor.

title: Genocide
description: Comparative and critical study of the modern phenomenon of genocide from religious, ethical and historical perspectives.

title: Topics Ancient Religion
description: Thematic study of specific sociological, literary or theological theme across the religious traditions of the ancient Mediterranean/Near East: Greek and Roman religions, Judaism, Christianity, Zoroastrianism, Manichaeism, etc. Topics may include creation, sacrifice, priesthoods, prophecies, holy books, the afterlife.

title: Human Rights
description: Introduction to the interdisciplinary study of the origins, evolution, denial and protection of Human Rights.

title: Topics in Jainism
description: Thematic study of specific periods, literary movements, sects and important figures within Jainism from a ranges of disciplinary perspectives.

title: Topics in Buddhism
description: Thematic exploration of historic developments, periods, regions and sects in Buddhism from an interdisciplinary perspective.

title: Human Rights and Gender
description: Gender and sexuality in the context of human rights. Topics include women's participation in the public sphere, the right to change gender, the right for family privacy, and the right to marriage.

title: Topics in Hinduism
description: Thematic study of specific periods, movements, leaders, regions, ethics or philosophies within Hinduism from an interdisciplinary perspective.

title: Christian Theology
description: Historical and systematic introduction to Christian doctrine, with attention to divergent traditions and the problem of orthodoxy and heresy.

title: New Test: Synoptic
description: Life and thought of the early Church as reflected by the Synoptic TraditionMatthew, Mark, Luke and Acts. Offered every third year to alternate with 141B, 141C.

title: New Test Lit: John
description: Life and thought of the early Church as reflected by the Johannine Tradition; the Gospel and letters of John. Offered every third year to alternate with courses 141A and 141C.

title: New Test Lit: Paul
description: Life and thought of the early Church as reflected by the Pauline traditionthe letters of Paul. Offered every third year to alternate with 141A, 141B.

title: Tyndale & English Bible
description: Study of Tyndale's New Testament translation as a literary and cultural monument in the context of previous Biblical translation, the historical situation in the 16th century, and the influence of this version on the English language and its literature.

title: New Testament Apocrypha
description: Extra-canonical Christian writings and their reception, from antiquity to the present. Emphasis on the importance of New Testament figures both as literary characters and as authors within different Christian traditions.

title: History of the Bible
description: History of the formation of the Christian biblical canon, with emphasis on differences between Christian traditions; survey of translations and adaptations of the Bible in and outside of Western Christianity; and brief history of issues in biblical interpretation.

title: Cntmp Amr Religion
description: Examination of several major movements and phenomena in 20th-century American religion.

title: Religious Ethics
description: Study of the religious bases to ethics through concentration on the ethical tracts of one major tradition, or through a comparison of the attitudes of two or more traditions to a common ethical issue.

title: Justice in MDH
description: Global issues of justice, equity, and fairness in healthcare and biomedical research. Emphasis on issues of race, gender, paternalism, and genetic privacy. Texts include scholarly articles, fiction, and film.

title: Religion & Medicine
description: Cross-cultural approach to the relationship between Religion and Medicine from earliest times to the present. How specific religious and philosophical worldviews have shaped and continue to shape attitudes toward physical and mental health.

title: The Hindu Temple
description: Comparative history of architecture and symbolism of the Hindu Temple in India, Southeast Asia and the United States. Attention to the temple as expression of religious knowledge, political authority, and cultural heritage through the lens of colonialism and postcolonialism.

title: Bhakti to 1200 CE
description: Exploration of Indian devotional traditions through literary, visual, and performance culture. Emphasis on period up to 1200 CE in southern India.

title: Bhakti from 1200 CE
description: Indian devotional traditions through literary, visual, and performance culture. Emphasis on period 1200 CE to the present.

title: Performing Arts in India
description: Survey of religion and performing arts in India. Emphasis on the influence of colonialism, nationalism, and regionalism on the history of Indian performing arts.
prerequisite: RST 030; RST 068; or Consent of Instructor.

title: Hindu Women & Goddesses
description: Hindu goddesses and the religious lives of Hindu women in India and the diaspora.

title: The Ramayana
description: Exploration of the Indian epic, Ramayana, through the lens of literature, performance, and visual art. Emphasis on the text's diversity and its contemporary global relevance. Topics include Ramayanas in Southeast Asia, and in various South Asian diaspora communities.

title: Mahabharata
description: Survey of the Indian epic, the Mahabharata, through textual, oral, and visual culture.

title: Intro Islamic Thought
description: The development of Islamic thought from the first centuries of Islam to the 18th century. Theology, philosophy, ethics, Sufism, historiography, political theory, fundamentalism, al-Farabi, al-Ghazzali, Ibn Rushd, Tusi, Ibn al-Arabi, Rumi, Molla Sadra, Ibn Khaldun, Ibn Abd al-Wahhab.

title: Modern Islam
description: The response of Islam to modernity: secularism, reformism, fundamentalism. Islam and imperialism, women, media and immigration. Islamic modernism, political Islam, Islam in Europe and America.

title: Modern Islam Auth/Tradit
description: Survey of Islamic thought, social organization, politics from 18th century through present. Focus on changing notations of moral authority and tradition. Concentration on Middle East and South Asia with sustained treatment of North American engagements with the Islamic world.

title: Intro Islamic Law
description: The development of Islamic law in the formative centuries of Islam, ca. 600-1000, as well as its adaptation to changing economic, social, and political conditions in subsequent periods. Legal schools, legal theory, the Shari'a, reformist movements, human rights.

title: Social Life of Islam
description: Introduction to culture and social life in Muslim societies. Focus on the plurality of traditions in Muslim faith, reason, and everyday practice. Special attention to Muslim rituals, ethical values, verbal genres, family life, sexuality and veiling, and youth culture.

title: Islam in Asia
description: Islam as a lived religion in the Indian sub-continent, Central Asia, China, and Southeast Asia. Emphasis is on primary sources studied comparatively and historically.

title: Buddhism
description: Buddhism in its pan-Asian manifestations, from its beginning in India to its development in Sri Lanka and Southeast Asia, Central Asia, China and Japan; teachings and practices, socio-political and cultural impact.

title: Buddhist Art
description: A historical survey of Buddhist art in relation to the development of Buddhist doctrine and philosophy.

title: Daoist Traditions
description: English-language survey of key Daoist texts and scholarship. Topics include Daoist concepts of the cosmos, the natural world, scripture, the body, and immortality; Daoist divinities; Daoism and the state.
prerequisite: A course in Chinese history recommended.

title: India Pop Religious Art
description: Survey of Indian popular religious art in prints, trade labels, comics and photographs.

title: Hindu Gods & Symbols
description: A historical survey of the development of the language of symbolism and iconography in Hinduism.
prerequisite: RST 068: Hinduism or RST 069: Hindu Mythology recommended, but not required.

title: Elementary Russian
description: Introduction to Russian grammar and development of all language skills in a cultural context with special emphasis on communication.

title: Elementary Russian
description: Continuation of grammar and language skills developed in RUS 001.

title: Elementary Russian
description: Continuation of grammar and language skills developed in course 2.

title: Intermediate Russian
description: Grammar review and conversational practice.

title: Intermediate Russian
description: Grammar review. Introduction to literature. Conversational practice.

title: Intermed Russian
description: Grammar review. Intermediate conversation and continued reading of literature.

title: Russia Today & Tomorrow
description: Examination of basic issues that pertain to the former totalitarian superpower which is in transition to democracy, the conflicts in Russia, its civilization and intellectual history up to including the present day and its tendencies for the future.

title: 19 C Russ Lit/Engl
description: Introduction to dominant literary trends, major literary figures and landmarks of Russian prose and poetry from the period of Sentimentalism through Romanticism and Realism to the beginnings of Modernism.

title: 20 C Russ Lit/Engl
description: Introduction to major literary trends such as Symbolism, Acmeism, Futurism, Neorealism, and Socialist Realism. Readings from representative representative writers such as Gorky, Bely, Pasternak, Solzhenitsyn, and Tertz.

title: Russ Children's Lit
description: Knowledge of Russian not required. History and theory of childrens literature, with special reference to Russian and Soviet examples. Analysis of genres, technique, and folklore elements, contrasted with those of the West. Students will write their own literature for children.

title: Russian Fantasy
description: Genres of fantasy and science ficton in Russian literature from pre-revolutionary to post-Soviet times. Topics include the role of science and the supernatural in literature, history and types of science fiction.

title: Advanced Russian
description: Topics in Russian grammar for the advanced student. Reading and discussion of journalistic texts and classic and contemporary literature. Conversation exercises utilizing literary and colloquial variants of current Russian speech.

title: Advanced Russian
description: Continuation of RUS 101A. Topics in Russian grammar for the advanced student. Reading and discussion of journalistic texts and classic and contemporary literature. Conversational exercises utilizing literary and colloquial variants of current Russian speech.

title: Advanced Russian
description: Continuation of RUS 101B. Topics in Russian grammar for the advanced student. Reading and discussion of journalistic texts and classic and contemporary literature. Conversational exercises utilizing literary and colloquial variants of current Russian speech.

title: Russian Composition
description: Practice in writing Russian. One composition on a different topic each week. Topics include: history, geography, politics, and literature of Russia; comparison of Russian and American lifestyles; current events. Conducted in Russian.

title: Adv Russian Conver
description: Intensive conversational practice and discussion based on current events and contemporary texts.

title: Topics Rus Lit and Cultu
description: Knowledge of Russian not required. Investigation of significant themes and issues of Russian literature and culture within their European context.
prerequisite: Upper division standing or consent of instructor.

title: 19th C Prose
description: Development of prose from Pushkin and Gogol, through Dostoevsky and Tolstoy, to Maxim Gorky. Other writers are selected sequentially: Turgenev, Goncharov, Pisemsky, Saltykov, Chekhov. Romanticism, the Natural School, critical realism, and psychological realism are covered. Conducted in Russian.

title: 19th C Rus Lit
description: Study of Russian literature (prose fiction, drama, poetry) from the period between 1800 and the end of the 19th century. May include authors like Pushkin, Lermontov, Gogol, Turgenev, Dostoevsky, Tolstoy, Chekhov. Offered alternately in English or Russian.
prerequisite: RUS 101C when offered in Russian; no prerequisite when offered in English.

title: 20th C Prose
description: Examination of various trends including Symbolism, Neorealism, and Socialist Realism in development of prose. Readings from such writers as Bely, Gorky, Sholokhov, Pasternak, Solzhenitsyn and others. Conducted in Russian.

title: 20th C Russian Lit
description: Study of Russian literature (prose, drama, poetry) from the period between 1900 and the end of the 20th century. May include authors like Y. Olesha, M. Bulgakov, D. Kharms, and L. Petrushevskaia. Offered alternately in English or Russian.
prerequisite: RUS 101C when offered in Russian; no prerequisite when offered in English (every other year).

title: Russian Theater
description: The main works of Russian dramatists from Fonvizin to the present, including Gogol, Turgenev, Tolstoy, Ostrovsky, Chekhov, Blok, Mayakovsky, Kharms. Conducted in Russian.

title: 19th C Rus Poetry
description: Introduction to the principles of Russian versification followed by historical and poetic analysis of the following figures: Derzhavin, Zhukovsky, Pushkin, Delvig, Baratynsky, Lermontov, Nekrasov, Tjutchev, and Fet. Conducted in Russian.

title: 20th C Rus Poetry
description: Introduction to principles of Russian versification followed by historical and poetic analysis of the following figures: Brjusov, Blok, Akhmatova, Mandelshtam, Esenin, Mayakovsky, Khlebnikov, Pasternak, Evtushenko, Voznesensky, and Brodsky. Conducted in Russian.

title: Russian Film
description: History of Russian film; film & social revolution, the cult of Stalin, dissident visions; film & the collapse of the Soviet empire; gender and the nation in Russian film. Taught in English; Russian films with English subtitles.

title: Contemp Russian Culture
description: Current trends in Russian culture and the relationship between artists and the government. Topics include recent changes in the cultural scene, postmodernist trends in literature, visual art, film, and theater.

title: Lit Of Revolution
description: Study of impact of revolution on society and culture; the major artistic, political and historical works surrounding the Russian revolutions of 1905 and 1917.

title: Post-Soviet Literature
description: Major authors and trends in Russian literature in post-1991 period. Discussion of impact of economic, social, and cultural turmoil of post-Soviet period on literary marketplace. Analysis of development of literary postmodernism in Russia.

title: Humor/Comedy in Russia
description: Survey of humor, comedy and satire in Russian culture, from the nineteenth-century to the present day. Includes literature, film, drama, and contemporary media. All works are situated in the historical and political context of Imperial Russia, the Soviet Union, and contemporary Russian society.

title: Pushkin's Eugene Onegin
description: Detailed analyses of Pushkin's novel Eugene Onegin; its style, syntax, and links to Russian History and culture.

title: Pushkin
description: The course covers three major periods of Pushkin's poetical works: his early Lyceum verse; his poetry of the early 1820s; and the mature period. The course also includes Pushkin's prose fiction, drama, and journalism.

title: Dostoevsky (In Eng)
description: Reading and analysis of Dostoevskys principal works such as Crime and Punishment, The Idiot, The Brothers Karamazov, and The Diary. Study of social and political views as reflected in Dostoevskys works.

title: Tolstoy (In English)
description: Study of Leo Tolstoys literary evolution and moral quest. Readings include his Confession, a major novel such as War and Peace or Anna Karenina, and representative shorter fiction.

title: Women in Russian Culture
description: An examination of Russian womens autobiography from the 18th through the 20th centuries, emphasizing the way in which the genre of autobiography serves as a means of the writers creation of herself, as opposed to her definition by others.

title: Chekhov (in English)
description: Examination of the literary and political writings of the major Russian dissident in the biographical context in which they were created. Knowledge of Russian not required.

title: Christ and Literature
description: Consideration of the intersection of literature, culture, and (at times heretical/"blasphemous") theology in Russia and elsewhere. Analysis of texts; discussion of historical contexts and related philosophical approaches to the New Testament.

title: Russian Culture
description: Knowledge of Russian not required. Study of Russian culture in nineteenth and twentieth centuries. Brief introduction of the beginnings up to nineteenth century. Russian art, music, philosophy, church, traditions, and daily life.

title: Censorship in Russia
description: Literature and censorship in Russia. Personal responsibility of the author vs. conformism to state morality. Russian myths and Russian realities.

title: Russian Folklore
description: Knowledge of Russian not required. Russian folklore, rituals, and history will be analyzed and compared with folklore of other peoples. Sociological implications of attitudes toward family unit, children, etc. Influences of folklore on Russian literature and historiography.

title: Yiddish Literature
description: Major writers of Yiddish in English translation; major genres of Yiddish literature from the mid-19th century to the present.

title: Sexuality Russ Lit
description: Sexuality in Russian oral and written literature from a dual, feminist-psychoanalytic perspective. Monogamy, free love, sexism, homosexuality, incest, androgyny, and others as depicted by such writers as Pushkin, Gogol, Tolstoy, Dostoevsky, Akhmatova, Blok, Tolstaia, and others.

title: Irrig for Urban Envir
description: Basic design, installation, and operation principles of irrigation systems for turf and landscape: golf courses, parks, highways, public buildings, etc. Emphasis on hardware association with sprinkler and drip/trickle systems.

title: Critical Inquiry
description: Contemporary issues, including global population trends, economic and environmental changes, cultural diversity and biodiversity, nutrition and food safety, fiber and textiles, changing consumer cultures. Inquiry processes emphasize ethics, multiple disciplines, and multiple perspectives.

title: Feeding the World
description: Scientific principles and dynamic interactions involved in food production, food processing, nutrition, shelf life and marketing from differing viewpoints. Physical, biological and social science issues influencing the availability and safety of the food supply worldwide.

title: Feeding the World
description: Scientific principles and dynamic interactions involved in food production, food processing, nutrition, and agribusiness. Physical, biological and social science issues influencing the availability and safety of the food supply worldwide.

title: Science, Tech & Society
description: Impact of developments in science and technology on the individual in society and how economics, politics, culture and values affect technological development.

title: Water in Popular Culture
description: Importance of water in many aspects of society as revealed through a survey of its depictions in film.

title: Water in Popular Culture
description: Analysis of the social construction of modern popular culture and its handling of the environment, focusing on water, as revealed through a survey of Hollywood and independent films.

title: Discovery:Sci & Society
description: Highlights a current issue and/or controversy found in contemporary society and looks at how this problem impacts and is affected by the physical, social and biological sciences. Topics vary.

title: Terrorism & War
description: Exploration of terrorism and war from science and social sciences perspectives. Terrorist cells and groups; biological, chemical, nuclear, and environmental terrorism; intelligence gathering and espionage; military strategy; genocide; epochal wars; clash of civilizations; nation building; and future global scenarios.

title: Terrorism & War
description: Terrorism and war from science and social sciences perspectives: terrorism (terrorist cells, WMD's, religious extremism), warfare (military strategy, genocide), and statecraft (diplomacy, clash of civilizations, epochal wars).

title: Water Quality at Risk
description: Natural and human threats to water quality. Balance of science and policy in all aspects of attaining, maintaining, and managing water quality, water contamination. Decoding popular media coverage of water quality and water contamination.

title: Crisis in Environment
description: Explores contemporary environmental issues by examining the causes, effects and solutions to a wide range of environmental problems facing the global ecosystem. Integrated discussion of political, societal and economic impact linkages with environmental problems. May be taught abroad.

title: Water, Power, Society
description: Water resources issues. How water has been used to gain and wield socio-political power. Water resources development in California related to current and future sustainability of water quantity and quality. Roles of science and policy in solving water problems.

title: California Geography
description: Introduction to cultural/societal patterns of California and their relationship to natural resources, biomes,geomorphology, and physiography. Focus on diversity of California's environments and their impacts on and alterations by human activities. Environmental issues in the State.

title: Plants & Society
description: Dependence of human societies on plant and plant products. Plants as resources for food, fiber, health, enjoyment and environmental services. Sustainable uses of plants for food production, raw materials, bioenergy, and environmental conservation. Global population growth and future food supplies.

title: Disease & Society
description: Introduction to the concept of disease, the societal and personal impacts of past, present and future diseases, and the science behind disease discoveries, causes, evolution, diagnosis, treatment, and prevention.

title: Forests & Society
description: Sociology, natural history and current issues of the world's forests. Application of scientific principles in outdoor laboratories and on-campus field trips.

title: AIDS and Society
description: Biology of HIV transmission and AIDS and how a biological agent acts on and influences the structure of contemporary society. Includes the psychology of risk and stigma, gender issues, changes in social relationships and public policy, global implications.

title: Extraterrestrial Soils
description: Introduction to the field of soil science and associated societal issues through an extraterrestrial lens. Importance of soils in the planetary and space sciences. Current societal challenges related to extraterrestrial soils with a specific emphasis on in situ resource utilization and planetary protection.

title: GIS & Society
description: Geographic Information Systems (GIS) as a spatial technology and a tool for change in society. Evaluate physical, biological and social impact of GIS in the context of case studies such as land, water and community planning.

title: Genetics & Society
description: Basic concepts of genetics, modern methods of biotechnology, the process of scientific discovery and the public perception of the process; present and future impact of genetics on society.

title: Global Climate Change
description: Causes of global climate change and the biological, geophysical, and social consequences of such change. Methods used by different scientists for predicting future events. Complexity of global affairs. Decision making under uncertainty.

title: Global Climate Change
description: Causes of global climate change and the biological, geophysical, and social consequences of such change. Methods used by different scientists for predicting future events. Complexity of global affairs. Decision making under uncertainty.

title: Mushroom, Mold, Society
description: Fungi as organisms with which humans interact daily, societal issues arising from these interactions. Fungi in medicine, religion, agriculture, and industry, as well as cultural perceptions of fungi.

title: Photography, Art & Scien
description: Photography is used to explore the common ground between art and science. Photographic processes, creativity and aesthetics, chaos and order, principles of space, time and light. Photographic interpretation and documentation of the natural world. Camera required.

title: UnderstandingPerformance
description: Relevance of theatre and performance to modern culture, science and society. Approaches to theatre/dance/media/performance art, integrated into Mondavi Centre for the Arts and Theatre and Dance Department programs.

title: Earth, Water, Sci, Song
description: Fusion of water and soil science with performing arts. Creative communication of scientific concepts and facts through exercises in song writing and poetry. Design, discuss and conduct public performances related to the functioning of the natural world.

title: Energy,Materials,Design
description: Global history of design across time, viewed through the lens of the effects of the creation and discovery of new energy sources, processes, and materials on design.

title: Genetic Engin Med Ag Law
description: Historical and scientific study of the impact of genetic engineering in medicine, agriculture, and law, including examination of social, ethical, and legal issues raised. Offered in a distance-learning format.

title: Env Chng Dis & Pub Hlth
description: Analysis of environmental changes from pre-history to the present and their influence on disease distribution, virulence and public health. Focus on critical study of many human-driven environmental changes and the accelerated transformation/spread of pathogens under globalization.

title: Applications Evolution
description: Applications of evolutionary biology in medicine, human behavior, and agriculture. Examination of the imprint of evolution on the human life cycle from conception to death.

title: Sci & Contemp Soc Issues
description: Study of a contemporary societal issue/problem emphasizing critical thinking with information drawn from several disciplines. Multiple instructors illustrate the necessity of an interdisciplinary and cooperative approach in solving important issues. Topics will vary.

title: Global Poverty
description: Social science and engineering analysis of causes and effects of world poverty and of policies to reduce it via economic growth, foreign aid, and community-level interventions; e.g., in potable water, sanitation, lighting, small scale energy, irrigation, health and microfinance.

title: Contemporary Leadership
description: Leadership, including issues, skills, and practices as they relate to individuals, organizations, diverse social settings and communities. Written and verbal communications, personality styles for collaborative work, and ethics.

title: Biodiversity & Society
description: Biodiversity in social context of South Africa; race, politics and conservation; use of indigenous plants and animals; weeds; water issues; ecotourism. Weekend and other field trips.
prerequisite: Acceptance into the Quarter Abroad Program "Biodiversity & Conservation in South Africa" and attendance in South Africa.

title: Genetics & Social Issues
description: Social issues arising from the development and use of modern methods of biotechnology. Presentation, evaluation, and critical discussions of the present and future impact of genetics on society.

title: Digital Communications
description: Use digital media to communicate a succinct, compelling story. In lecture, discussion and activities, create storyboards and scripts, use video, audio, and editing technology, and produce a short media-rich video to effectively convey a message.

title: Intro Sociology
description: Principles and basic concepts of sociology. The study of groups, culture, collective behavior, classes and caste, community and ecology, role, status, and personality.

title: Intro to Sociology
description: Principles and basic concepts of sociology. The study of groups, culture, collective behavior, classes and caste, community and ecology, role, status, and personality.

title: Self & Society
description: Principles and basic concepts of sociological social psychology. Includes the study of the character of the self, identity, roles, socialization, identity change, emotion and social interaction.

title: Social Problems
description: General sociological consideration of contemporary social problems in relation to sociocultural change and programs for improvement.

title: Social Problems
description: General sociological consideration of contemporary social problems in relation to sociocultural change and programs for improvement.

title: Immigration
description: Social and demographic analysis of immigration: motives and experiences of immigrants; immigration and social mobility; immigration, assimilation, and social change; multicultural societies. Detailed study of immigration into the U.S., with comparative studies of Europe, Australia, and other host countries.

title: Global Social Change
description: Introduction to change and diversity in world history, including the United States. Examines population and family, technological change and economic development, power and status, culture and identity.

title: Health & Illness
description: Introduction to the sociology of health and illness, including social determinants of health, social inequalities in health/health disparities, social construction of health, the organization of health care, and the politics of health care reform.

title: Race & Ethnicity
description: Introduction to the sociology of race and ethnicity in the U.S., including historical changes in racial and ethnic categories, mechanisms of racism, anti-racist social movements, the role of social policy in shaping patterns of racial inequality.

title: Labor
description: Labor and employment issues in the contemporary United States with some use of historical and comparative materials. Topics include strategies pursued by employers and employees, labor market discrimination and the role of social policies in shaping labor markets.

title: Data Visualization
description: Introduction to quantitative data across the social sciences (Communications, Political Science, Psychology, Sociology, and other disciplines). Transforming data, describing data, producing graphs, visual reasoning, and interpretations.

title: Popular Culture
description: Social mechanisms that shape modern popular culture. High, folk, and mass culture: historical emergence of popular culture. Mass media, commercialization, ideology and cultural styles. Theories and methods for analyzing cultural expressions in pop music, street art, film, television, and advertising.

title: Popular Culture
description: Social mechanisms that shape modern popular culture. High, folk, and mass culture: historical emergence of popular culture. Mass media, commercialization, ideology and cultural styles. Theories and methods for analyzing cultural expressions in pop music, street art, film, television, and advertising.

title: Multicultural Societies
description: Macro-structural analysis of contemporary multicultural societies; immigration and assimilation in comparative perspective; social construction of racial and ethnic group identities; ethnicity and gender; group conflict and cooperation; controversies surrounding multiculturalism. First course in a two-course Multicultural Immersion Program.

title: Multicultural Societies
description: Social-psychological analysis of personal experiences living in a multicultural society; conforming to or rejecting group identity or stereotypes; managing and reducing conflict; cross-cultural communication; promises and problems of diversity at UC Davis. Second course in a two-course Multicultural Immersion Program.

title: Intro Social Resrch Meth
description: Examination of logic and methods of sociological research. Selection and definition of problems of investigation, data-gathering techniques, and sampling.

title: Intro Social Rsch
description: Examination of the methodological problems of social research. Selection and definition of problems of investigation, data-gathering techniques, and sampling.

title: Int Social Research
description: Data-analysis techniques, measurement, scaling, multivariate analysis, and quantitative measures of association.

title: Intro to Social Stats
description: Data-analysis techniques, measurement, scaling, multivariate analysis, and quantitative measures of association.

title: Intro to Social Stats
description: Data-analysis techniques, measurement, scaling, multivariate analysis, and quantitative measures of association.

title: Sociological Theory
description: The origins of modern sociological thought. Special emphasis on three major theorists from the classical tradition of nineteenth century European social thought: Karl Marx, Max Weber, and Emile Durkheim.

title: Sociological Theory
description: Origins of modern sociological thought. Special emphasis on three major theorists from the classical tradition of 19th-century European social thought: Karl Marx, Max Weber, and Emile Durkheim.

title: California Society
